subject: Quarterly settlement flow & make-good proposal for hosted usage
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@brightwave.io>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightwave.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quarterly settlement flow & make-good proposal for hosted usage

Hi Jamie / Alex —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. As promised, I wanted to put our proposal for quarterly settlement (true-up) mechanics and the make-good cadence in writing so your finance/procurement teams have a single place to review. Attachment: 2027Q1-usage-buckets.xlsx (usage detail by route).

High-level proposal (draft):
- Commit basis: BrightWave commits to a hosted API spend band for Q2 (committed token bucket).
- Quarterly true-up: At the end of each quarter we compare committed bucket vs actual per-token usage.
- Make-goods (shortfalls): If BrightWave under-utilizes the committed bucket, Redwood issues a make-good credit (credit note) equal to the unused committed dollars. Credits are applied to the next invoice cycle.
- Overages: Any usage beyond the commit is billed at the agreed overage rate for that quarter.
- Timing: Draft credit issuance timeline: preliminary statement within 15 days after quarter close; credit applied within 45 days (invoice adjustment).
- Conversion option: Customer may elect to convert accrued credits into an amendment that increases committed capacity (i.e., add committed bucket) with a discount applied prospectively if executed before the start of the next quarter.

Open items we flagged on the call: proration rules for partial-quarter sign-ups, whether credits can be counted toward future commit thresholds, and whether unused credits should roll forward. I captured suggested defaults in the attached makegood-schedule-draft.pdf.

Can you confirm whether BrightWave prefers: (A) credits applied as invoice-only (no rollover / do not count toward future commits) or (B) allow credits to be applied to future commit calculations (counts toward next-quarter commitment)? Option (A) is our standard; (B) is possible with procurement/legal sign-off.

Next steps: if you’re comfortable with the draft, we’ll prepare an amendment and push a DocuSign link for countersign. If you want different treatment for credits/rollover, we can surface that as a one-off in the amendment.

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Sales (Hosted)
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — quick clarifying questions from our side:
1) Proration: We go live mid-quarter for Q2 — will the preliminary true-up compare the full committed bucket or prorate to our go-live date?
2) Credits: If a credit is issued can our procurement team request it be applied as a payment (i.e., reduce the invoice total) vs. a credit on account? We prefer payment reductions where possible for audit simplicity.
3) Rollover: Ideally we can roll unused credits into the next quarter; is that only for enterprise customers or standard?

Jamie
VP, Finance
BrightWave

Jamie — great questions. Picking these up and adding a few operational constraints from Billing/Revenue Ops: 

1) Proration: For mid-quarter go-lives we will prorate committed buckets to the actual active days in the quarter (standard practice). The attached spreadsheet shows a prorated example under the "Proration" tab.

2) Credit mechanics: We can offer credits as either (a) invoice-level reductions (preferred for audit/close), or (b) on-account credits that sit in BrightWave's Redwood ledger. For most customers we do invoice-level reductions for the quarter immediately following the true-up. We will mark the credit as a negative line item replacing a separate on-account credit flow.

3) Rollover: Default policy: credits do NOT roll forward automatically and do NOT count toward future commit thresholds. Rollover or counting credits toward a future commit requires an explicit contractual amendment.

4) Timing & GL impact: We need finance to confirm acceptance of a 45-day post-quarter credit application window (Billing will post the adjustment in the next billing cycle). Also need BrightWave's GL code for the credit line so we can map the reduction.

5) Make-good alternatives: If BrightWave would prefer rollover, we can provide a one-time concession: convert the unused committed dollars into a committed bucket increase (amendment) with discount tiers applied prospectively — this requires countersign before month-end and will be backdated for pricing only if agreed in writing.

Let us know which option (invoice reduction vs on-account credit; rollover allowed vs no) you prefer and we’ll fold it into the amendment text.

—Ben
Head of Billing & Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference

Looping Procurement/Legal expectations on language and timing. A couple of internal asks before we send the DocuSign: 
- Procurement: if BrightWave chooses the rollover option we need an explicit SOW language block and final sign-off by Redwood Legal. That will likely add 7–10 business days to the timeline.
- Finance: please confirm the GL mapping and whether invoice-level reductions are acceptable for accounting (Ben already flagged this).
- Ops: when amendment is ready, please include a table showing (a) committed bucket, (b) actual usage, (c) credit calculation, (d) the timing of application. The attached spreadsheet should be sufficient for now.

Proposed operational timeline if BrightWave accepts standard defaults (no rollover; invoice reduction):
1) 4/15 — Redwood sends amendment + DocuSign link.
2) 4/22 — BrightWave countersign (requested).
3) 6/30 — Q2 quarter end; preliminary statement issued within 15 days.
4) ~8/14 — Credit applied (within 45 days).

If BrightWave wants rollover or credits to count toward future commits, call out early — we’ll need procurement/legal early in the loop.

Thanks,
Laura

- Proration: committed buckets will be prorated for mid-quarter go-live dates.
- Credits: Redwood will issue invoice-level credit reductions (preferred for audit).
- Rollover: credits do NOT roll forward and do NOT count toward future commit thresholds unless we execute a formal amendment.
- Timing: preliminary true-up within 15 days post-quarter; credit applied within 45 days post-quarter.

Options for BrightWave (choose one):
A) Standard — invoice reduction, no rollover (fastest path, amendment sent today).
B) Rollover/Count-as-commit — requires procurement/legal sign-off and explicit SOW language; adds 7–10 business days.
